title: Quasiperiodicity
summary: A context-dependent form of recurrent nonperiodic behavior generated by multiple incommensurate periods or frequencies.
assumptions: F:T^k→X is periodic in each angular coordinate, where T=R/(2πZ).
ω in R^k is a frequency vector.

content.human: Quasiperiodic motion can be built from several periodic motions whose frequencies never line up into one common period.
content.exact: In this record, f:R→X is quasiperiodic when f(t)=F(ω_1 t,...,ω_k t) for a function F on the k-torus and a frequency vector ω whose components are rationally independent: if m in Z^k and m·ω=0, then m=0.
content.example: f(t)=cos(t)+cos(sqrt(2)t) is a standard quasiperiodic example under this convention.
content.caveat: “Quasiperiodic” has other precise meanings in tilings, symbolic dynamics, cocycles, and other areas. Those require separate records rather than silently reusing this definition.

verification.method: Definition checked for internal consistency; not yet linked to an external formal proof artifact.
